# The generated API, shape by shape

Every snippet below is the Kotlin the processor emits, taken from a generated file. Types are
written fully qualified in the output; they are shortened here only where the line would wrap.

## The file

```kotlin
// Generated by dev.modaal:mocks-processor. DO NOT EDIT.
// Regenerated at test compilation; generated output is never committed.
package dev.modaal.mocks.receipt

class ReceiptEnvironmentMock(
  staticConfig: ReceiptConfig,
) : ReceiptEnvironment {
```

The class is public, named `<Interface>Mock`, and declared in the interface's own package. Its
constructor carries one parameter per read-only requirement that has no guessable default, and
nothing else.

Members are emitted name-sorted, whatever order the interface declares them in, and the rendering
reads no clock, no unstable-ordered map and no absolute path — the same interface always produces the
same bytes.

## A method with one recordable parameter

```kotlin
override fun log(message: kotlin.String) {
  logCallCount += 1
  logArgs.add(message)
  logHandler?.invoke(message)
}
var logCallCount: kotlin.Int = 0
val logArgs: kotlin.collections.MutableList<kotlin.String> = mutableListOf()
var logHandler: ((kotlin.String) -> kotlin.Unit)? = null
```

The count and the argument are recorded **before** the handler runs, so a handler that throws does
not un-make the call.

## A method with several recordable parameters

Kotlin has no tuple, so the record is a nested data class named after the method:

```kotlin
data class MeasureArgs(
  val width: kotlin.Int,
  val height: kotlin.Int,
)
override fun measure(width: kotlin.Int, height: kotlin.Int, onDone: (kotlin.Int) -> kotlin.Unit): kotlin.Boolean {
  measureCallCount += 1
  measureArgs.add(MeasureArgs(width, height))
  measureHandler?.let { return it(width, height, onDone) }
  return false
}
val measureArgs: kotlin.collections.MutableList<MeasureArgs> = mutableListOf()
var measureHandler: ((kotlin.Int, kotlin.Int, (kotlin.Int) -> kotlin.Unit) -> kotlin.Boolean)? = null
```

A test asserts on it by value:

```kotlin
assertEquals(listOf(ReceiptEnvironmentMock.MeasureArgs(width = 4, height = 3)), environment.measureArgs)
```

`onDone` is function-typed, so it reaches the handler and stays out of the record. A method whose
parameters are all function-typed, and a method with no parameters, get no `<fn>Args` member at all —
assert through the handler and the call count.

## A suspend method, and what an unset handler does

```kotlin
override suspend fun load(id: kotlin.String): ReceiptConfig {
  loadCallCount += 1
  loadArgs.add(id)
  loadHandler?.let { return it(id) }
  error("loadHandler expected to be set.")
}
var loadHandler: (suspend (kotlin.String) -> ReceiptConfig)? = null
```

`suspend` is carried into the handler's type. The fallback rules, in the order the generated code
applies them:

| the return type | what an unset handler returns |
| --- | --- |
| `Unit` | nothing; the handler is invoked if set and the method returns |
| `Flow<E>` | `<fn>Channel.receiveAsFlow()` |
| any nullable type | `null` |
| a type with a guessable default | that default |
| anything else | fails with `IllegalStateException` carrying `<fn>Handler expected to be set.` |

The guessable defaults:

| type | default |
| --- | --- |
| `Int`, `Long`, `Double`, `Float` | `0`, `0L`, `0.0`, `0.0f` |
| `Boolean` | `false` |
| `String` | `""` |
| `List`, `Map`, `Set` | `emptyList()`, `emptyMap()`, `emptySet()` |
| `MutableList`, `MutableMap`, `MutableSet` | `mutableListOf()`, `mutableMapOf()`, `mutableSetOf()` |

A nullable return therefore never fails an unseeded test:

```kotlin
override fun findLabel(id: kotlin.String): kotlin.String? {
  findLabelCallCount += 1
  findLabelArgs.add(id)
  findLabelHandler?.let { return it(id) }
  return null
}
```

## A method returning `Flow`

```kotlin
override fun events(): kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow<ReceiptEvent> {
  eventsCallCount += 1
  eventsHandler?.let { return it() }
  return eventsChannel.receiveAsFlow()
}
val eventsChannel: kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel<ReceiptEvent> =
  kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel(kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel.UNLIMITED)
```

The channel is unlimited, so a test may send before anyone collects. `receiveAsFlow()` completes when
the channel closes, and only then:

```kotlin
environment.eventsChannel.trySend(ReceiptEvent.Tick(1))
environment.eventsChannel.close()
assertEquals(listOf(ReceiptEvent.Tick(1)), environment.events().toList())
```

Seeding `eventsHandler` takes precedence and needs no close. Only an exact `Flow<E>` return gets a
channel; a nullable `Flow<E>?` falls back to `null`.

## Properties

```kotlin
// var requirement: stored, and writes are counted. Construction does not count.
override var volume: kotlin.Double = 0.0
  set(value) {
    volumeSetCount += 1
    field = value
  }
var volumeSetCount: kotlin.Int = 0

// read-only requirement with a guessable default: a var override a test can re-seed.
override var idleTimeoutMs: kotlin.Long = 0L

// read-only requirement without one: a constructor parameter.
override var staticConfig: ReceiptConfig = staticConfig

// read-only Flow property: counted reads, a get handler, and the channel fallback.
override val configUpdates: kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow<ReceiptConfig>
  get() {
    configUpdatesGetCount += 1
    configUpdatesGetHandler?.let { return it() }
    return configUpdatesChannel.receiveAsFlow()
  }
var configUpdatesGetCount: kotlin.Int = 0
var configUpdatesGetHandler: (() -> kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow<ReceiptConfig>)? = null
val configUpdatesChannel: kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel<ReceiptConfig> = …
```

There is no `<prop>GetCount` for a stored property — a read of a stored `var` is not counted.

An interface of properties alone generates a constructor-seeded bag:

```kotlin
val dependency = ReceiptDependencyMock(config = config)   // `step: Double` defaulted to 0.0
```

Adding a member without a guessable default to such an interface breaks every construction of the
mock at compile time, which is the point of seeding through the constructor.

## Overloads

Overloads would collide on the shared bookkeeping names. The overload with the fewest parameters
keeps the plain name; each other overload appends its capitalized parameter names:

```kotlin
fun update(id: String)                → updateCallCount, updateArgs, updateHandler
fun update(id: String, force: Boolean) → updateIdForceCallCount, updateIdForceArgs, updateIdForceHandler
```

Adding a wider overload later therefore does not rename the members an existing test already uses.

## Inherited requirements

The mock implements the interface's full requirement set, inherited members included. A member with
an interface-default body keeps its default and gets no mock members.

## The same vocabulary in the Swift twin

A codebase that tests the same logic on both platforms gets one dialect. The Swift side is generated
by swift-sourcery-templates.

| Kotlin | Swift |
| --- | --- |
| `<fn>CallCount` | `<method>CallCount` |
| `<fn>Args` | `<method>Args` |
| `<fn>Handler` | `<method>Handler` |
| `<prop>GetCount`, `<prop>GetHandler` | `<var>GetCount`, `<var>GetHandler` |
| `<prop>SetCount` | `<var>SetCount` |
| `<fn>Channel` for a `Flow` member | `<method>Subject` for an `AnyPublisher` member |
| `<fn>Handler expected to be set.` | the same string |
| constructor-seeded bag | the initializer-seeded equivalent |

Members with no counterpart here: the Swift generator also emits `<method>CancelCallCount` for a
member returning a cancellation token, and takes per-declaration annotations that this processor has
no equivalent for, because targets are selected in the build script.

The names, the channel-backed stream shape and the failure string are shared deliberately. Renaming
one of them is a change to both generators, not a local refactor.
